thread:
ashley: kicking off an FP8 crossfire sweep on H100 + L40S overnight. goal: confirm kernel selection stability + calibration delta. leaving traces on for 6h.

ashley: quick summary so far — L40S is stable. H100 runs show intermittent 20–35% p95 latency spikes after KV cache grows past ~60k keys. spikes co-occur with kernel fallback messages in logs. :thinking_face:

matt: can you paste the fallback log lines?

ashley: sure — here's the relevant section from the runtime log (trimmed):
```
[2026-02-15T03:42:19Z] kernel_election: selected te.fp8_gemm_v2
[2026-02-15T03:42:19Z] transformer_engine: fp8_autocast=true, calibration_state=stable
[2026-02-15T03:42:22Z] kernel_election: fallback to te.int8_gemm_v1 (reason=precision_underflow_rate>threshold)
[2026-02-15T03:42:22Z] kv_cache: size=61523, hit_rate=0.72, eviction=low
[2026-02-15T03:42:22Z] latency: p50=7.8ms p95=46.2ms p99=112.6ms
```

raj: interesting — fallback says precision_underflow_rate. that suggests the FP8 calibration stats are drifting under heavy KV cache warm paths (longer context). did you capture TE (transformer-engine) counters?

ashley: yes, brief dump from TE counters at the moment of fallback:
```
TE_FP8_STATS { scale_max: 1.12, scale_min: 0.03, underflow: 128, overflow: 2 }
TE_INT8_STATS { underflow: 0, overflow: 0 }
KERNEL_CTR { fp8_matmul: 4123, int8_matmul: 19 }
```

raj: so FP8 is used most of the time, but under long-KV cache traces we see underflow counts rising. could be accumulation/scale decay with long prefix KV replays.

sara: is the model using per-tensor or per-channel scaling? we had a previous bug where per-tensor scaling drifted faster with repeated small prefix updates.

ashley: per-tensor. the deploy that turned on a more aggressive KV prefetch was 2269873001 (recent infra change). could be related.

matt: ran a microbench on an identical model with synthetic KV replay (60k keys) — results:
- force FP8 kernel: p50=6.9ms p95=38.7ms, underflow=95
- allow fallback: p50=6.9ms p95=52.1ms, underflow spikes then switch to INT8, p95 after switch=74.5ms

matt: also captured kernel timing by name on H100: fp8_matmul avg=1.15ms, int8_matmul avg=2.6ms. fallback cost is ~2x for the matmul plus extra copy/format overhead.

raj: so the latency spike isn't from matmul speed per se but from the fallback path + runtime switch cost. how often does it flip back to FP8?

ashley: usually it stays on INT8 for 10–30s before conditions let it try FP8 again. multiple flaps in a short window cause long-tail.

matt: hypothesis: aggressive KV prefetch + sustained long-context patterns cause FP8 scale matrices to hit low dynamic range -> underflows -> fallback. calibration window may be too small to adapt.

raj: possible mitigations:
- increase TE calibration window or enable exponential smoothing of scales
- change to per-channel scaling for linear layers that see KV accumulation
- change batching heuristics to avoid big contiguous prefetch bursts (throttle microbatch ramp)

ashley: tried bumping calibration window from 128->512 steps in a dev build. reduced underflow counts by ~60% but runtime still falls back in some traces. p95 improved but not fully resolved.

sara: can we replay the exact request series that triggers the fallback? if we repro deterministically we can add targeted unit tests.

ashley: yes — saved a compressed trace (s3://redwood-perf/2271004567/trace.tar.gz). upload includes runtime profile, TE counters, nvprof summaries.

infra-bot: deploy scheduled: rollout/2270-kernel-mux-tuning at 2026-02-15T09:00Z (canary 5%).

matt: for immediate experiments i tried forcing kernel selection with --runtime-override kernel=te.fp8_gemm_v2 during the sweep to avoid fallback. result: stable FP8 but quality regressions on a small eval set (some token-level shifts).

raj: that matches expectation — forcing avoids fallback but may produce low-precision outputs in edge cases. need to balance perf and accuracy.

sara: what's the tradeoff if we instead force a near-term soft-fallback: when underflow rate crosses X, we drop microbatch size by 1 for N requests instead of switching to INT8. cheaper than kernel switch.

matt: tried microbatch throttle: reducing microbatch per-device from 8->6 during detect window. p95 drop improved 25% and underflows fell. but throughput also dropped ~8%.

ashley: collecting additional telemetry for the next 12h: per-model layer-wise fp8 underflow rates, kernel election timestamps, KV prefetch bursts. planning to try per-channel scaling on the top-k linear layers tomorrow.

raj: another angle — L40S doesn't show this because kernel implementation has a slightly larger accumulator width in te.fp8_gemm_v2_l40 variant. could we port that accumulator behavior to H100 kernel?

matt: chatted with runtime/llvm folks — the H100 kernel uses fused multiply path that kept accumulator narrower to reduce memory traffic. widening it may cost a little throughput but reduce numeric edge cases.

ashley: opened a PR (internal) to add a tunable accumulator width flag: runtime flag --fp8-accum-width=(16|32). default remains 16. will land to canary tomorrow.

sara: also include a new metric: kernel-flip-count per minute. this will help triage flappy election issues.

ashley: agree. adding to telemetry. also attaching a short flamegraph snippet from the worst 30s window (te attached):
```
flamegraph (peak window):
  runtime_dispatch (40%)
  kernel_mmu_copy (12%)
  te.fp8_gemm_v2 (22%)
  fallback_path/config_swap (18%)
  other (8%)
```

raj: summary action items:
- ashley: continue collecting traces + try per-channel scaling experiment (A)
- matt: prototype fp8-accum-width flag on H100 kernel (B)
- sara: add kernel-flip-count metric & microbatch throttle A/B test (C)
- infra: hold wide rollout until next canary completes and we have mitigation data

deploy-bot: rollout/2270-kernel-mux-tuning canary paused (manual hold) by infra team.

ashley: thanks everyone — will post results from per-channel run tomorrow. :thumbsup:
